state.seed_assertion: Controllers must conduct a data protection impact assessment before processing when the processing is likely to result in high risk to rights and freedoms, particularly when using new technologies and considering the nature, scope, context and purposes of the processing.

sentences.1: Controllers must conduct a data protection impact assessment before processing when the processing is likely to result in high risk to rights and freedoms, particularly when using new technologies and considering the nature, scope, context and purposes of the processing.
sentences.10: A DPIA must assess the origin, nature, particularity and gravity of risks to the rights and freedoms of data subjects.
sentences.2: Where a type of processing in particular using new technologies, and taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of the processing, is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall, prior to the processing, carry out an assessment of the impact of the envisaged processing operations on the protection of personal data.
sentences.3: A data protection impact assessment is required when processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects.
sentences.4: If you have determined that the processing is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of data subjects, you must carry out a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) for each processing operation.
sentences.5: A DPIA may also be carried out on a voluntary basis in order to identify and deal as effectively as possible with the risks, even if they are minor, to the rights and freedoms of individuals.
sentences.6: The measures and safeguards provided to protect the rights and freedoms of data subjects under the GDPR;
sentences.7: Rights and freedoms of natural persons refer mainly to data protection and privacy, but also include other fundamental rights such as freedom of speech, freedom of thought, and freedom of movement.
sentences.8: The reference to the rights and freedoms of natural persons refers mainly to data protection and the protection of privacy but also, where appropriate, to other fundamental rights, such as freedom of speech, freedom of thought, freedom of movement, prohibition of discrimination, the right to freedom and freedom of conscience and religion.
sentences.9: Potential impacts on the rights and freedoms of data subjects are identified in case of events such as illegitimate access to data, an unwanted modification of data or their disappearance
